digest.component_or_area: observability marker emissions (voter, merge, reconcile, artifact)
propositions: Line-start marker tokens (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, RECONCILE_DEGRADED, ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR, LLM_TOKEN_USAGE) are emitted twice: once via logger.error/info/warning and once via print to stderr, because configure_logging attaches a StreamHandler that outputs logged messages to stdout, and journald merges stdout and stderr into a single stream that the anchored probe then counts twice.

The observability probe grep anchors (e.g., `grep -cE '^VOTER_ERROR \{'` at infra/scripts/observability.sh:166) match both the logger-emitted copy and the stderr-printed copy, doubling the reported metric (voter_errors doubled every real error; MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR live-doubled; RECONCILE_DEGRADED, ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR, LLM_TOKEN_USAGE latently doubled).

Unconfigured logging (NullHandler path) produces exactly one countable line per error via the print-to-stderr fallback, demonstrating the fallback is correct and the double emission is caused by the interaction of dual emission + logging config.

The fix is to retain print(line, file=sys.stderr) as the sole line-start marker emission (the fail-safe that works in both configured and unconfigured states) and change the logger copies to emit only the structured record body json.dumps(record) without the token prefix, matching the shape already used by _emit for non-marker events.

The dual emission construct (token-prefixed marker string passed to both a logger call and stderr print) must be prevented from reappearing via a structural class-guard test that scans src/rebar for the pattern.

commit b0ac2544720 (ticket c130-6a87-531e-4441) wired configure_logging's stdout StreamHandler, activating the second line-start emission path for markers that had shipped with unconditional stderr prints, making the regression triggered by the logging config change.
